unresolved_added: The Summary offers a complete network-to-policy story, but budget, occupancy and HR-health outputs remain internal simulation claims.
The 85% occupancy, middle-level churn and salary/loyalty clues are qualitative task inputs, not an observed longitudinal personnel dataset.
Churn-rate notation uses a monthly formula without fully stating units, while directed affiliation, shortest paths and alpha normalization lack disconnected-edge policy.
The cooperation compactness sum uses friendship intensity beta without a source, range, or empirical edge-strength calibration.
The seven-level allocation and evenly placed vacancies are presented as reasonable but are not validated against actual staffing.
Training recursions use xi coefficients and the fixed 18% baseline without fitting, bounds, seed, or a demonstrated relation between training and churn.
Productivity is a constructed proxy from efficiency, base productivity and working time; its units and observed business outcome are absent.
Monte Carlo churn is described as random, but probability assignment, seed, event order and high-middle boundary are not reproducibly frozen.
Promotion ranks working time and uses maximum productivity as eligibility, while tie handling, cross-division choice and threshold units are unspecified.
Recruitment assumes a median time, lowest-productivity hire and a vacancy-proportional plan without releasing rates, costs or raw event histories.

The baseline working-rate path fluctuates around 85% then stabilizes near 80%, and ten simulations report 26.22 sigma recruitment plus 140.15 sigma training, but cost provenance and uncertainty are missing.
The 25% and 35% paths cross below 80% by months 12 and 4 and end near 75% and 67%; this is a three-scenario simulation, not an external threshold test.
The no-external-recruitment comparison improves working rate slightly but lowers middle-level enthusiasm after month 10, exposing a policy tradeoff rather than a single best action.
The 14-person, three-layer network and adjacency tensor are illustrative; layer edges, cross-layer coupling and whole-company outcomes are not observed.
Table 1 reports internal degree, clustering, path length and density; the recommendation for more data and scientific team division is not a causal result.
Six-run stochastic error has maximum magnitude below 0.015, but the signed grouping formula, run count and no uncertainty propagation limit the claim.
Changing attenuation 0.90/0.93/0.95/0.97 and growth 1.05/1.07/1.10/1.13 yields local insensitivity claims without raw paths or a declared tolerance.
The strengths infer realistic quantification and common-sense agreement, while weaknesses omit division-operation networks and retirement/temporary absence.
The conclusion restates a complete workflow but adds no independent validation beyond the model's own simulations and illustrations.
